question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

I wish we had ______ come here.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. never.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The structure "I wish + had + V3 (past perfect)" expresses a regret about a past action. The speaker regrets having come to this place, so the negative adverb "never" fits perfectly.

◦ Correct: I wish we had never come here. (काश हम यहाँ कभी न आए होते)

• "Never" is placed between the auxiliary "had" and the past participle "come" — the standard position for a mid-sentence adverb of frequency.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "right" — "had right come" is ungrammatical; "right" is not an adverb of negation.

• Option 2 "clear" — "had clear come" is meaningless.

• Option 4 "agreed" — "had agreed come" is wrong; it would need "had agreed to come".

NOTE

• Uses of "wish":

◦ Wish + past simple → regret about the present (I wish I knew the answer).

◦ Wish + past perfect → regret about the past (I wish we had never come here).

◦ Wish + would → irritation / desire for change (I wish you would stop shouting).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Carnal
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Spiritual.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Carnal" means relating to the body and its physical/sensual desires; fleshly, worldly. (शारीरिक / दैहिक)

◦ Example: The saint warned his disciples against carnal pleasures.

• Its direct antonym is "Spiritual", meaning relating to the soul or spirit rather than the body. (आध्यात्मिक)

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Material" (relating to physical things/matter) is closer to a synonym of carnal than an antonym.

• Option 3 "Temporal" means worldly/secular or relating to time — again worldly, not spiritual.

• Option 4 "Somatic" means of the body — an exact synonym of carnal, hence the opposite of what is required.

NOTE

• Synonyms of carnal: fleshly, sensual, bodily, physical, somatic, worldly.

• Antonyms of carnal: spiritual, chaste, moral, pure, ascetic.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Fail to function normally
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Malfunction.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Malfunction" means to fail to work or function in the normal or correct way. (ठीक से काम न करना / खराबी)

◦ Example: The engine began to malfunction halfway through the journey.

• The prefix "mal-" means bad/wrong, and "function" means to work — so mal + function = to work badly.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Maltreat" = to treat someone cruelly or badly (दुर्व्यवहार करना).

• Option 2 "Mangle" = to damage something by crushing or tearing it badly.

• Option 3 "Manipulate" = to control or influence cleverly, often unfairly.

NOTE

• Common "mal-" words: malnutrition (bad nourishment), malpractice (wrong professional conduct), malicious (spiteful), malady (a disease), maladroit (clumsy).

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given phrase.

All of a sudden
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Quickly and unexpectedly.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "all of a sudden" means very quickly and without any warning; suddenly and unexpectedly. (अचानक / एकाएक)

◦ Example: All of a sudden, the lights went out and the hall fell silent.

• The key idea in the phrase is the element of surprise — the event was not anticipated.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Intentionally" (deliberately) is the opposite idea — a sudden event is not planned.

• Option 3 "Quickly and Expectedly" contradicts the phrase, because "sudden" implies the event was not expected.

• Option 4 "Accidently" (a misspelling of "accidentally") means by chance, which is not the same as suddenly.

NOTE

• Similar expressions: "out of the blue", "in the blink of an eye", "without warning", "on a sudden impulse".

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My daughter was / invited to lunch / hosted by the Governor / at his residence.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. invited to lunch.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Names of meals (breakfast, lunch, dinner) normally take no article — "We had lunch at two."

• But when the meal is particularised/qualified by a describing phrase or clause, the indefinite article "a" is required. Here "lunch" is qualified by "hosted by the Governor", so it must be "invited to a lunch".

◦ Correct: My daughter was invited to a lunch hosted by the Governor at his residence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Segment 1 "My daughter was" is a correct subject + verb (passive) opening.

• Segment 3 "hosted by the Governor" is a correct past-participle phrase modifying "lunch".

• Segment 4 "at his residence" uses the correct preposition "at" for a place.

NOTE

• Compare: "We had dinner at eight." (no article) vs "We attended a dinner given in his honour." (qualified — article needed). The same rule applies to "a lunch hosted by...", "a breakfast arranged by...".

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Rectifie.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rectifie" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Rectify", which means to put something right; to correct an error. (सुधारना / ठीक करना)

◦ Example: The bank promised to rectify the mistake in my statement.

• Spelling key: REC + TI + FY — the word ends in "-fy", not "-fie".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Resist" (to oppose or withstand), "Recruit" (to enrol new members/soldiers) and "Repulse" (to drive back; to repel) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Verbs ending in "-fy": rectify, classify, justify, notify, magnify, satisfy. The "-ie" spelling appears only in the past form: rectify → rectified, and in the noun rectification.

question:
Select the option that rectifies the spelling of the underlined word in the given sentence.

The maintenence department did a fabulous job.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. maintenance.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The correct spelling of the underlined word is "maintenance", meaning the process of keeping something in good condition/repair. (रख-रखाव)

◦ Correct: The maintenance department did a fabulous job.

• Spelling key: MAIN + TEN + ANCE. Note that although the verb is "maintain", the noun drops the "i" and ends in "-ance", not "-ence".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mainteanance", Option 3 "maintenannce" (double "n") and Option 4 "meintenance" are all wrong spellings.

• The printed form "maintenence" is wrong because it uses "-ence" instead of "-ance".

NOTE

• Similar tricky "-ance" nouns: appearance, performance, resistance, acceptance, attendance. Compare with "-ence" nouns: existence, occurrence, persistence, independence.

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the bracketed word in the following sentence to fill in the blank.

The novel’s intricate plot and rich character development kept readers ________(committed) from the beginning to the end.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. engaged.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The bracketed word "committed" here means fully involved/absorbed and devoted to something. Its closest synonym in this context is "engaged", meaning deeply involved and holding one's interest and attention. (तल्लीन / जुड़ा हुआ)

◦ Correct: The novel's intricate plot and rich character development kept readers engaged from the beginning to the end.

• The context words "intricate plot" and "rich character development" show that the readers' interest was held throughout — exactly what "engaged" conveys.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "secluded" (kept away/isolated from others) is unrelated to interest.

• Option 3 "detached" (aloof, uninvolved) is the antonym of the required sense.

• Option 4 "dismantled" (taken apart, pulled to pieces) is used for machines/structures, not readers.

NOTE

• Synonyms of engaged (in this sense): absorbed, engrossed, involved, occupied, immersed, riveted. Antonyms: detached, uninterested, indifferent, aloof.

question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom.

These things are very hard to swallow.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. difficult to believe.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "hard to swallow" means difficult to believe or accept. It is used for statements, excuses or news that seem unconvincing or unpleasant. (विश्वास करने में कठिन)

◦ Example: His story about missing the flight twice was a bit hard to swallow.

• Here the sense is figurative, not literal — it has nothing to do with actually swallowing food.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 4 "difficult to eat" is the literal meaning and is therefore the trap option in an idiom question.

• Option 1 "difficult to resist" and Option 2 "difficult to speak" do not match the idiom at all.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "a bitter pill to swallow" (an unpleasant fact one must accept), "take it with a pinch of salt" (not to believe something completely), "swallow one's pride" (to accept humiliation).

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

The decision to go on a trip after my vacations was the ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. icing on the cake.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "the icing on the cake" means an extra benefit that makes a good situation even better. (सोने पे सुहागा)

◦ Correct: The decision to go on a trip after my vacations was the icing on the cake.

• "Icing" is the sweet layer spread over a cake — the cake is already good, and the icing makes it better; hence the figurative meaning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "ice on the cake", 3 "apple on the cake" and 4 "icing on the brownie" are distorted forms and are not accepted idioms. Idioms must be used in their fixed, unchanged form.

NOTE

• Similar idioms: "cherry on top" (an added bonus), "the best of both worlds", "a blessing in disguise". Opposite idea: "to add insult to injury" (to make a bad situation worse).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The new software / consists from / several features / and tools.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. consists from.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The verb "consist" is always followed by the preposition "of" when it means "to be made up of". "Consists from" is incorrect.

◦ Correct: The new software consists of several features and tools.

• Note also that "consist" is a stative verb — it is not normally used in the continuous form ("is consisting of" is wrong).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment 2 "several features" and Segment 4 "and tools" are correct plural noun phrases.

• Segment 3 "The new software" is correct — "software" is an uncountable noun (never "softwares").

NOTE

• Fixed verb + preposition combinations: consist of, comprise (no preposition), composed of, made up of, depend on, insist on, deprive of, accuse of. Remember: "comprise" is never followed by "of" — "The team comprises ten players.".

question:
Select the most appropriate idiom to fill in the blank.

It's easy to say that you'll start exercising every day, but it is ______________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. easier said than done.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "easier said than done" means much more difficult to do in practice than it sounds in words. (कहना आसान, करना मुश्किल)

◦ Correct: It's easy to say that you'll start exercising every day, but it is easier said than done.

• The sentence itself gives the clue: "It's easy to say ... but ..." — a clear contrast between speaking and doing.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "like a fish out of water" = feeling uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings.

• Option 3 "crying wolf" = raising a false alarm repeatedly so that no one believes you later.

• Option 4 "going the extra mile" = making a special effort beyond what is expected.

NOTE

• The conjunction "but" signals a contrast, so the missing idiom must oppose "easy to say" — only "easier said than done" does that.

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Paralycis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Paralycis" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "Paralysis", meaning the loss of the ability to move (and sometimes to feel) in part or most of the body. (लकवा / पक्षाघात)

◦ Example: The accident left him with partial paralysis of the legs.

• Spelling key: PARA + LY + SIS — the ending is "-sis", not "-cis".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Lyricist" (a writer of song lyrics), "Indigestion" (difficulty in digesting food) and "Patron" (a supporter/benefactor) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Medical nouns ending in "-sis": paralysis, diagnosis, analysis, thrombosis, tuberculosis. Their plurals change "-sis" to "-ses": paralyses, analyses, diagnoses. The related adjective is "paralytic" and the verb is "paralyse/paralyze".

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word given in brackets to fill in the blank.

Uncle Joe is ___________________(reputable) for spending 10 years of his youth in prison due to armed robbery.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. notorious.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Reputable" means having a good reputation; respected and trustworthy. (प्रतिष्ठित)

• Its antonym is "notorious", meaning famous for something bad — infamous. Since Uncle Joe spent ten years in prison for armed robbery, he is famous for a bad reason. (कुख्यात)

◦ Correct: Uncle Joe is notorious for spending 10 years of his youth in prison due to armed robbery.

• The collocation "notorious for + (bad deed)" is also grammatically perfect here.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "mournful" (very sad/sorrowful) and Option 2 "anxious" (worried) describe feelings, not reputation.

• Option 3 "well-known" is neutral/positive in tone and is closer to a synonym of reputable, so it cannot be the antonym.

NOTE

• Note the difference: famous (well known for something good) vs notorious/infamous (well known for something bad). Antonyms of reputable: notorious, infamous, disreputable, discreditable, shady.

question:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

If you work hard, you secure good marks.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. you secure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• This is a Conditional Type 1 sentence (a real/probable future condition). Its correct structure is:

◦ If + Subject + V1 (present simple), Subject + will + V1

• The "if-clause" here is "If you work hard" (present simple), so the main clause must use "will secure", not the present simple "secure".

◦ Correct: If you work hard, you will secure good marks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• "If you" and "work hard" correctly form the conditional clause in the present simple.

• "good marks" is a correct object phrase.

• Remember the golden rule: never use "will" in the "if" clause of a Type 1 conditional.

NOTE

• The three main conditionals:

◦ Type 1 (real future): If it rains, we will cancel the match.

◦ Type 2 (unreal present): If it rained, we would cancel the match.

◦ Type 3 (unreal past): If it had rained, we would have cancelled the match.

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who is skilled in making maps
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Cartographer.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "Cartographer" is a person who is skilled in drawing or making maps and charts. (मानचित्रकार)

◦ Example: The cartographer spent months mapping the coastline.

• The study/art of map-making is called "cartography" (from the French "carte" = map).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Calligrapher" = a person skilled in beautiful handwriting (calligraphy).

• Option 2 "Curator" = a person in charge of a museum or its collection.

• Option 3 "Cacographer" = a person with bad handwriting or bad spelling (the opposite of a calligrapher).

NOTE

• Other useful one-word substitutes: Geographer (one who studies the earth's surface), Cosmographer (one who maps the universe), Topographer (one who describes the physical features of a place), Philatelist (a stamp collector), Numismatist (a coin collector).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

Sita loves her glass container in which she has many fish.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. aquarium.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• An "aquarium" is a glass tank/container filled with water in which fish and other water creatures are kept. (मछलीघर)

◦ Correct: Sita loves her aquarium.

• The word comes from the Latin "aqua" meaning water.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "cannister (canister)" = a small metal or plastic container for tea, flour, gas, etc. — not for fish.

• Option 3 "planetarium" = a building/room where images of stars and planets are projected on a dome.

• Option 4 "museum" = a building where objects of historical, artistic or scientific interest are displayed.

NOTE

• Related "-arium/-orium" words: aquarium (water animals), vivarium (living animals), terrarium (small land plants/animals), herbarium (dried plants), sanatorium (a place for recovering patients), auditorium (a hall for an audience).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can rectify the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to rectify it, select ‘no rectification needed’.

His claim to be the smartly kid in the school was a bit hyperbole!
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. smartest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Smartly" is an adverb, but the blank comes before the noun "kid", where an adjective is required. So the adverb must be replaced.

• The definite article "the" before the slot and the phrase "in the school" (comparison within a whole group) demand the superlative degree — "the smartest".

◦ Correct: His claim to be the smartest kid in the school was a bit hyperbole!

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "no rectification needed" is wrong because an adverb cannot modify the noun "kid".

• Option 3 "smarter" is the comparative and would need "than" (smarter than the others), not "the ... in the school".

• Option 4 "smart" (positive degree) does not suit "the ... in the school", which calls for a superlative.

NOTE

• Degrees of comparison: smart – smarter (than) – the smartest (in/of). Use the superlative with "the" when one member is compared with all others in a group: "the tallest boy in the class", "the best player in the team".

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Easily set on fire
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Inflammable.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Inflammable" means easily set on fire; capable of burning quickly. (शीघ्र ज्वलनशील)

◦ Example: Petrol is highly inflammable, so smoking is banned near fuel pumps.

• Important: "inflammable" and "flammable" mean the same thing. Here "in-" comes from "inflame" (to set on fire) and is not a negative prefix. The true opposite is "non-inflammable".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Innocuous" = harmless, causing no injury or offence.

• Option 2 "Ingrained" = deeply fixed/firmly established (ingrained habits).

• Option 4 "Inimical" = hostile, unfriendly, harmful to something.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes: combustible (able to catch fire), incombustible / fireproof (unable to burn), volatile (evaporating rapidly), explosive (liable to blow up).

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error.

She has / bought / a car / two years ago.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. She has.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The adverbial "two years ago" refers to a definite/finished point in the past, so the sentence must be in the Simple Past tense, not the Present Perfect.

• The Present Perfect ("has bought") can never be used with a definite past-time expression such as "ago", "yesterday", "last year" or "in 2019". Hence the faulty segment is "She has".

◦ Correct: She bought a car two years ago.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Segment 2 "bought" is the correct past form / past participle of "buy" (buy – bought – bought) and stays unchanged.

• Segment 3 "a car" is a correct singular countable noun phrase.

• Segment 4 "two years ago" is a correct adverbial of past time.

NOTE

• Present Perfect goes with indefinite time markers: already, just, yet, ever, never, recently, so far, since, for.

• Simple Past goes with definite past markers: ago, yesterday, last night, in 1947, then.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. They read reference books in order to score good marks in the examination. This is the demanding (2)________ of all the students who are appearing in the examinations. But, most students feel tensed on the day before an examination. Everyone is in a state of (3)________ as to what questions would be asked in the paper and whether they could write their answers properly to get good marks. Such overthinking is the cause of (4)________ which definitely affects their performance. They should revise the subject regularly and should not keep their doubts pending. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. preparing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The blank follows the preposition-like conjunction "while" and precedes "for examinations". The fixed collocation is "to prepare for an examination" — to get ready for it by studying. (परीक्षा की तैयारी करना)

◦ Correct: Students put their heart and soul into studies while preparing for examinations.

• The very next sentence ("They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions ... preparing notes") confirms that the passage is about preparation.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "calculating" (working out by mathematics) does not collocate with "for examinations".

• Option 2 "guiding" (showing the way) would need an object — one guides somebody.

• Option 3 "producing" (manufacturing/creating) is entirely out of context.

NOTE

• Useful collocations: prepare for an exam, appear for/in an exam, sit for an exam, revise for an exam, score/secure marks, clear/crack an exam.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. They read reference books in order to score good marks in the examination. This is the demanding (2)________ of all the students who are appearing in the examinations. But, most students feel tensed on the day before an examination. Everyone is in a state of (3)________ as to what questions would be asked in the paper and whether they could write their answers properly to get good marks. Such overthinking is the cause of (4)________ which definitely affects their performance. They should revise the subject regularly and should not keep their doubts pending. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. routine.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "routine" is a regular, fixed way of doing things — a set daily schedule of activities. (दिनचर्या)

• The preceding lines describe activities repeated throughout the year (revisions, flash cards, notes, reference books). Such a repeated pattern of study is exactly a demanding routine.

◦ Correct: This is the demanding routine of all the students who are appearing in the examinations.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "principle" = a basic rule or belief — not a set of daily activities.

• Option 2 "method" = a particular way/procedure of doing one thing; it does not carry the sense of a regularly repeated schedule.

• Option 4 "habit" = an individual's automatic personal tendency; "the demanding habit of all the students" does not fit the description of a planned study schedule.

NOTE

• "Routine" collocates well with daily, strict, demanding, gruelling, fixed — e.g., "a gruelling training routine", "his daily routine".

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. They read reference books in order to score good marks in the examination. This is the demanding (2)________ of all the students who are appearing in the examinations. But, most students feel tensed on the day before an examination. Everyone is in a state of (3)________ as to what questions would be asked in the paper and whether they could write their answers properly to get good marks. Such overthinking is the cause of (4)________ which definitely affects their performance. They should revise the subject regularly and should not keep their doubts pending. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. uncertainty.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Uncertainty" means the state of not knowing or not being sure about something. (अनिश्चितता)

• The clause that follows — "as to what questions would be asked ... and whether they could write their answers properly" — expresses doubt about an unknown outcome, which is precisely uncertainty. The phrase "in a state of uncertainty" is also a natural collocation.

◦ Correct: Everyone is in a state of uncertainty as to what questions would be asked in the paper ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "confidence" and 3 "assurance" mean certainty/self-belief — the exact opposite of the doubtful mood described, and they clash with "most students feel tensed".

• Option 2 "hesitation" means a pause before acting out of unwillingness; the sentence is about not knowing the paper, not about pausing before an action.

NOTE

• Words for doubt: uncertainty, ambiguity, scepticism, apprehension, misgiving. Words for certainty: assurance, conviction, confidence, certitude.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. They read reference books in order to score good marks in the examination. This is the demanding (2)________ of all the students who are appearing in the examinations. But, most students feel tensed on the day before an examination. Everyone is in a state of (3)________ as to what questions would be asked in the paper and whether they could write their answers properly to get good marks. Such overthinking is the cause of (4)________ which definitely affects their performance. They should revise the subject regularly and should not keep their doubts pending. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. anxiety.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Anxiety" means a feeling of worry, nervousness or unease about an uncertain outcome. (चिंता / घबराहट)

• The passage says students "feel tensed" and are in a state of uncertainty; such "overthinking" naturally causes anxiety, which then harms performance. "Exam anxiety" is the standard expression.

◦ Correct: Such overthinking is the cause of anxiety which definitely affects their performance.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "agitation" means outward disturbance or public protest/restlessness; it does not fit the inner mental worry caused by overthinking as precisely as "anxiety".

• Options 3 "peace" and 4 "comfort" are positive words and contradict the negative effect stated — "which definitely affects their performance".

NOTE

• Synonyms of anxiety: worry, apprehension, unease, nervousness, disquiet, angst. Antonyms: calmness, composure, serenity, peace.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

Students put their heart and soul into studies while (1)________ for examinations. They prepare the syllabus by giving many revisions, making important points on flash cards, preparing notes throughout the year. They read reference books in order to score good marks in the examination. This is the demanding (2)________ of all the students who are appearing in the examinations. But, most students feel tensed on the day before an examination. Everyone is in a state of (3)________ as to what questions would be asked in the paper and whether they could write their answers properly to get good marks. Such overthinking is the cause of (4)________ which definitely affects their performance. They should revise the subject regularly and should not keep their doubts pending. This will not create a (5)________ of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. burden.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "burden" is a heavy load, especially a duty or responsibility that is hard to bear. The expression "a burden of backlog" (the pressure of pending, unfinished work) is the natural choice here. (बोझ)

◦ Correct: This will not create a burden of backlog and they will get sufficient time to resolve their problem.

• The advice given — revise regularly and do not keep doubts pending — is meant to prevent work from piling up, i.e., to avoid a burden.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "mass" (a large quantity of matter) and Option 3 "weight" (how heavy something physically is) are physical/literal words and do not collocate with "backlog".

• Option 4 "power" (strength/authority) is positive and completely out of context.

NOTE

• Collocations with burden: bear/carry a burden, ease/lighten the burden, a financial burden, the burden of proof, a burden of responsibility.

question: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded a reform organisation in 1875 that attempted to reform Hinduism. What was it called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arya Samaj.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj in 1875 at Bombay (Mumbai). Its headquarters were later shifted to Lahore. (आर्य समाज — 1875)

• The Arya Samaj gave the slogan "Back to the Vedas" and worked against idol worship, caste rigidity, child marriage and untouchability, while supporting widow remarriage, women's education and the Shuddhi movement (reconversion to Hinduism).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Swami Dayanand's famous book is "Satyarth Prakash" (The Light of Truth), written in Hindi.

• Prarthana Samaj — founded in 1867 at Bombay by Atmaram Pandurang, with M. G. Ranade and R. G. Bhandarkar as leading members.

• Satyashodhak Samaj — founded in 1873 at Pune by Jyotirao Phule for the upliftment of the lower castes.

• Brahmo Samaj — founded in 1828 at Calcutta by Raja Ram Mohan Roy, the "Father of the Indian Renaissance".

NOTE

• The Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) schools and colleges grew out of the Arya Samaj movement, blending modern (English) education with Vedic values.

question: The Brihadeswara Temple at Tanjavur built by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajaraja I.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Brihadeeswarar (Brihadeswara) Temple at Thanjavur (Tanjavur), Tamil Nadu, was built by the Chola ruler Rajaraja I in about 1010 CE. It is also known as the Rajarajeswaram or the "Big Temple". (बृहदेश्वर मंदिर — राजराज प्रथम)

• It is dedicated to Lord Shiva and is a masterpiece of Dravidian architecture, famous for its towering vimana (about 216 ft) and a huge monolithic Nandi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The temple is part of the UNESCO World Heritage listing "Great Living Chola Temples", along with the temples at Gangaikonda Cholapuram and Airavatesvara Temple, Darasuram.

• Rajendra Chola I, son of Rajaraja I, built Gangaikonda Cholapuram and led naval expeditions to Southeast Asia.

• Samudragupta was a Gupta emperor (4th century CE), praised in the Allahabad Pillar (Prayag Prashasti) inscription of Harisena.

NOTE

• Chola art is also renowned for its bronze sculptures, especially the famous Nataraja (dancing Shiva) images.

question: Which diseases result from a deficiency of Vitamin B due to its insufficient intake?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beri Beri.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Beri Beri" is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin B1 (Thiamine). It affects the nervous system (dry beriberi) and the heart (wet beriberi), causing weakness, numbness in the limbs and swelling. (बेरी-बेरी — विटामिन B1 की कमी)

• Rich sources of Thiamine: whole grains, unpolished rice, pulses, nuts and yeast. Eating highly polished rice is a classic cause of beriberi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Colour blindness is a genetic (hereditary) disorder of the eye, not a vitamin deficiency.

• Rickets (soft, bent bones in children) is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin D.

• Scurvy (bleeding gums, slow wound healing) is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid).

NOTE

• Other B-vitamin deficiency diseases: B2 (Riboflavin) → cheilosis/cracks at the corners of the mouth; B3 (Niacin) → pellagra; B9 (Folic acid) and B12 (Cyanocobalamin) → anaemia. B-complex and C are water-soluble vitamins; A, D, E and K are fat-soluble.

question: What is the minimum voting age for the citizens of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18 years.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The minimum voting age in India is 18 years. It was reduced from 21 years to 18 years by the 61st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1988 (which came into effect in 1989), amending Article 326. (मताधिकार की न्यूनतम आयु — 18 वर्ष)

• Article 326 provides for elections to the Lok Sabha and the State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Minimum ages for offices: MLA/MP (Lok Sabha) — 25 years; Rajya Sabha/MLC — 30 years; President/Vice-President — 35 years.

• Elections in India are conducted by the Election Commission of India (Article 324), established on 25 January 1950 — celebrated as National Voters' Day.

NOTE

• The 61st Amendment is often called the "Voting Age Amendment"; it was passed during the tenure of Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi.

question: Who among the following singers had a Guinness World Record for recording 28 songs in a single day? (As of December 2022.)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kumar Sanu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The celebrated Bollywood playback singer Kumar Sanu holds the Guinness World Record for recording 28 songs in a single day (in 1993). (कुमार सानू — 28 गाने एक ही दिन में)

• His real name is Kedarnath Bhattacharya; he was born in Kolkata and was given the name "Kumar Sanu" by the music director Jagjit Singh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kumar Sanu won the Filmfare Award for Best Male Playback Singer for five consecutive years (1991–1995) — a record — and was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2009.

• Sonu Nigam, Udit Narayan and Arijit Singh are also leading playback singers; Udit Narayan received the Padma Bhushan (2016).

NOTE

• Legendary Indian playback singers with Guinness recognition include Lata Mangeshkar and Asha Bhosle, both noted for recording a very large number of songs.

question: ‘Anandamath’ is a famous ________ novel which was written by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bengali.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Anandamath" (1882) is a famous Bengali novel written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay (Chatterjee). (आनंदमठ — बांग्ला उपन्यास)

• The novel is set against the background of the Sanyasi Rebellion of the late 18th century in Bengal and contains the song "Vande Mataram".

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• "Vande Mataram" was adopted as the National Song of India on 24 January 1950. It was first sung at the 1896 Calcutta session of the Indian National Congress by Rabindranath Tagore.

• Other works of Bankim Chandra: Durgeshnandini, Kapalkundala, Devi Chaudhurani, Rajmohan's Wife (his only English novel).

NOTE

• The National Anthem "Jana Gana Mana" was written by Rabindranath Tagore in Bengali and adopted on 24 January 1950; it takes about 52 seconds to sing.

question: The four Nattuvanars namely Ponaiyah, Vadivelu, Sivanandam and Chinnaiya, who are renowned as Tanjaore Bandhu shaped up the modern day ___________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharatanatyam.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The four Nattuvanars (dance masters) — Ponnaiah, Vadivelu, Sivanandam and Chinnaiah — known as the "Tanjore Quartet (Tanjore Bandhu / Thanjavur Brothers)", re-organised and shaped modern Bharatanatyam in the early 19th century, during the reign of Serfoji II of Thanjavur. (भरतनाट्यम)

• They fixed the present margam (concert order) of a Bharatanatyam recital: Alarippu → Jatiswaram → Shabdam → Varnam → Padam → Tillana.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance of Tamil Nadu, based on Bharat Muni's Natya Shastra; its revival in the 20th century is credited to Rukmini Devi Arundale and E. Krishna Iyer.

• Kuchipudi — Andhra Pradesh; Kutiyattam (Kodiattam) — Sanskrit theatre of Kerala (a UNESCO Intangible Heritage); Kathakali — the story-play dance-drama of Kerala.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms recognised by the Sangeet Natak Akademi: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya.

question: In February 2023, Uttar Pradesh government launched a/an _____ called Family ID-One Family One Identity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Portal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In February 2023, the Uttar Pradesh government launched the "Family ID – One Family One Identity" portal (familyid.up.gov.in). (परिवार आईडी पोर्टल — उत्तर प्रदेश)

• The portal creates a unique 12-digit family identity number for every family in the state so that welfare schemes, ration and employment benefits can be delivered in a targeted, transparent way.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Families already holding a ration card are automatically issued the Family ID using their ration-card number; others can register on the portal.

• The Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh at the time of launch was Yogi Adityanath; the state capital is Lucknow.

NOTE

• A similar scheme, "Parivar Pehchan Patra (PPP)", was launched earlier by the Haryana government for family-based delivery of welfare benefits.

question: Which of the following statements is best related to the ‘pacific ring of fire’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Known for volcano and earthquakes.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Pacific Ring of Fire" (also called the Circum-Pacific Belt) is a horseshoe-shaped belt around the Pacific Ocean that is famous for frequent volcanic eruptions and earthquakes. (प्रशांत महासागरीय अग्नि वलय)

• About 75% of the world's active volcanoes and roughly 90% of the world's earthquakes occur here, because it lies along the convergent boundaries and subduction zones of tectonic plates.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Countries/regions on the Ring of Fire: Japan, Indonesia, the Philippines, New Zealand, Chile, Peru, Mexico and the western USA (California, Alaska).

• The other major earthquake belt is the Mid-Continental (Alpine-Himalayan) belt, which includes the Himalayas.

NOTE

• Instruments: earthquakes are recorded by a seismograph; their magnitude is measured on the Richter scale and intensity on the Mercalli scale. The study of earthquakes is seismology and of volcanoes is volcanology.

question: Why are intermediate goods NOT included in the calculation of national income?
option_1: Including intermediate goods would result in double counting.
option_2: Intermediate goods are not produced within the country's borders.
option_3: Including intermediate goods would decrease the value of national income.
option_4: Intermediate goods are not important for measuring economic activity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Including intermediate goods would result in double counting.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Intermediate goods are goods used as inputs in the production of other goods (e.g., wheat used to make flour, flour used to make bread). Their value is already included in the price of the final good.

• If they were counted separately as well, the same value would be counted twice or more, inflating national income. This error is called the "double counting problem". (दोहरी गणना की समस्या)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• To avoid double counting, economists either (i) count only final goods and services, or (ii) use the "value added method" — adding only the value added at each stage of production.

• Option 2 is wrong because intermediate goods are very much produced within the country; Option 3 is wrong because including them would increase (overstate) the figure; Option 4 is wrong because such goods do matter economically — they are simply not counted separately.

NOTE

• Key aggregates: GDP (produced within the domestic territory), GNP = GDP + net factor income from abroad, NNP = GNP – depreciation, and National Income = NNP at factor cost. In India, national income data is compiled by the NSO/CSO under MoSPI.

question: According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021,India’s rank is ________ out of 109 countries.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 66th.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the Global Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) 2021, India ranked 66th out of 109 countries. (वैश्विक बहुआयामी गरीबी सूचकांक 2021 — भारत 66वें स्थान पर)

• The Global MPI is published jointly by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI), University of Oxford.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The MPI measures poverty across three dimensions and 10 indicators:

◦ Health — nutrition, child mortality;

◦ Education — years of schooling, school attendance;

◦ Standard of living — cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets.

• In India, NITI Aayog publishes the National MPI, which uses the same three dimensions but 12 indicators (adding maternal health, bank accounts, etc.).

NOTE

• The MPI is "multidimensional" because it goes beyond income poverty and captures the overlapping deprivations a household actually experiences.

question: The tribal dancer and singer, Arjun Singh Dhurve from ________ has been conferred with ‘ Padma Shri’ in the year 2022.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Madhya Pradesh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Arjun Singh Dhurve, a noted tribal (Baiga) dancer and singer from Madhya Pradesh, was conferred the Padma Shri in 2022 in the field of Art. (अर्जुन सिंह धुर्वे — मध्य प्रदेश)

• He is known for popularising the Baiga tribal folk dance and songs of the Mandla/Dindori region of Madhya Pradesh.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Padma Awards — Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri — are announced every year on the eve of Republic Day (26 January) and presented by the President of India.

• Padma Shri is the fourth-highest civilian award of India (after the Bharat Ratna, Padma Vibhushan and Padma Bhushan); it was instituted in 1954.

NOTE

• Madhya Pradesh has the largest tribal population among Indian states; its major tribes include the Gond, Bhil, Baiga, Korku and Sahariya.

question: What is the main purpose of a bank statement?
option_2: To transfer funds to another account
option_4: To have locker facility in the bank
solution_text:
The correct answer is To track income and expenses.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "bank statement" is a periodic (usually monthly/quarterly) summary of all the transactions in an account — deposits (credits), withdrawals (debits), charges and the closing balance.

• Its main purpose is therefore to let the account holder track income and expenses, reconcile records and detect any unauthorised transaction. (बैंक विवरण — आय और व्यय का रिकॉर्ड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 is wrong — transferring funds is done through NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI or a cheque, not through a statement.

• Option 3 is wrong — advertising is a marketing activity, not the purpose of a statement.

• Option 4 is wrong — a locker is a separate safe-deposit facility hired from the bank.

NOTE

• Related terms: passbook (a booklet recording the same transactions), cheque (an order to pay), KYC (Know Your Customer), and NEFT/RTGS/IMPS/UPI — India's electronic payment systems regulated by the RBI/NPCI.

question: The Konark Dance Festival (KDF) has been held at Konark since 1986 between ___________ every year.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1st and 5th December.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Konark Dance Festival (KDF) has been organised at Konark, Odisha, since 1986, and is held every year from the 1st to the 5th of December. (कोणार्क नृत्य महोत्सव — 1 से 5 दिसंबर)

• It is held against the magnificent backdrop of the Konark Sun Temple, and features Odissi, Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Manipuri, Kuchipudi and Chhau performances.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Konark Sun Temple was built in the 13th century (c. 1250 CE) by King Narasimhadeva I of the Eastern Ganga dynasty. It is designed as a gigantic chariot of the Sun God (Surya) with 24 carved wheels and seven horses.

• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site (1984) and is popularly called the "Black Pagoda".

NOTE

• Other famous dance festivals of India: Khajuraho Dance Festival (Madhya Pradesh, February), Mamallapuram Dance Festival (Tamil Nadu) and the Elephanta Festival (Maharashtra).

question: Identify the southernmost range of the Himalaya from the following.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shiwaliks Range.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Shiwaliks (Outer Himalayas / Himachal) form the southernmost and lowest range of the Himalayas, with an average height of about 900–1,100 metres and a width of 10–50 km. (शिवालिक — सबसे दक्षिणी श्रेणी)

• They are made of unconsolidated sediments brought down by rivers from the main Himalayas.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• From north to south, the Himalayan ranges are:

◦ Trans-Himalaya (Karakoram, Ladakh, Zaskar) — the northernmost;

◦ Greater Himalaya (Himadri) — the highest, with Mt. Everest, Kanchenjunga, Nanga Parbat; contains the perpetual snowline;

◦ Lesser/Middle Himalaya (Himachal) — Pir Panjal, Dhauladhar, Mahabharat; hill stations like Shimla, Mussoorie, Nainital;

◦ Shiwaliks (Outer Himalaya) — the southernmost.

• The longitudinal valleys between the Shiwaliks and the Lesser Himalaya are called "Duns" (e.g., Dehra Dun, Kotli Dun, Patli Dun).

NOTE

• The Himalayas are young fold mountains, formed by the collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates; they act as a climatic barrier that blocks the cold Central Asian winds and traps the monsoon.

question: Which of the following statements about the Directive Principles of State Policy is NOT correct?
option_1: To secure suitable employment and a healthy working environment for men, women and children
option_2: To provide adequate means of livelihood for both men and women
option_3: To ensure equal pay for equal work for men only
option_4: To reorganise the economic system to prevent the concentration of wealth in a few hands
solution_text:
The correct answer is To ensure equal pay for equal work for men only.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are contained in Part IV (Articles 36–51) of the Constitution and are borrowed from the Constitution of Ireland. They are non-justiciable but "fundamental in the governance of the country" (Article 37). (राज्य के नीति निदेशक तत्व)

• Article 39(d) directs the State to secure "equal pay for equal work for both men and women" — not for men only. Hence the statement in Option 3 is incorrect, and it is the required answer.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The other three statements are correct DPSPs under Article 39:

◦ 39(a) — adequate means of livelihood for all citizens, men and women equally;

◦ 39(e)/39(f) with Article 42 — health and strength of workers (men, women and children) and just and humane conditions of work;

◦ 39(c) — the economic system should not result in the concentration of wealth and means of production to the common detriment.

NOTE

• DPSPs are classified as Socialistic (Arts. 38, 39, 41–43), Gandhian (Arts. 40, 43, 46, 47, 48) and Liberal-Intellectual (Arts. 44, 45, 48A, 49, 50, 51). Dr. B. R. Ambedkar called them a "novel feature" of the Constitution.

question: Which of the following events took place in 1919?
option_2: The Representation of the People Act was passed
option_3: The Thuggee and Dacoity Suppression Act was passed
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Rowlatt Act (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act) was passed in March 1919, allowing detention without trial. Mahatma Gandhi launched the Rowlatt Satyagraha in 1919 — his first all-India mass agitation. (रौलेट सत्याग्रह — 1919)

• The Act was popularly condemned as "No appeal, no vakil, no daleel". The protest movement led to the tragic Jallianwala Bagh massacre on 13 April 1919 at Amritsar, ordered by General Dyer.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Charter Acts were passed by the British Parliament in 1793, 1813, 1833 and 1853 — none in 1919.

• The Representation of the People Acts in India were passed in 1950 and 1951, providing for the conduct of elections.

• The Thuggee and Dacoity Suppression Acts were enacted between 1836 and 1848, associated with William Sleeman under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.

NOTE

• 1919 also saw the Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu–Chelmsford Reforms), which introduced dyarchy in the provinces, and Rabindranath Tagore's renunciation of his knighthood in protest against Jallianwala Bagh.

question: The novel ‘Train to Pakistan’ was written by ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Khushwant Singh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Train to Pakistan" (1956) was written by the eminent Indian author, journalist and historian Khushwant Singh. (ट्रेन टू पाकिस्तान — खुशवंत सिंह)

• The novel depicts the Partition of India (1947) through the story of the fictional border village of Mano Majra, showing how communal violence destroyed a peaceful, mixed community.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Other works of Khushwant Singh: I Shall Not Hear the Nightingale, Delhi: A Novel, The Company of Women, Truth, Love and a Little Malice (autobiography) and A History of the Sikhs.

• He was awarded the Padma Bhushan (1974) — which he returned in 1984 in protest against Operation Blue Star — and later the Padma Vibhushan (2007).

NOTE

• Other notable Partition literature: "Tamas" (Bhisham Sahni), "Azadi" (Chaman Nahal), "Ice-Candy-Man / Cracking India" (Bapsi Sidhwa) and the short story "Toba Tek Singh" (Saadat Hasan Manto).

question: Popular Bollywood actor Kriti Sanon is a trained __________ dancer.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The popular Bollywood actor Kriti Sanon is a trained Kathak dancer. (कथक)

• Kathak is the classical dance of North India (Uttar Pradesh); its name comes from "Katha" (story) and "Kathakar" (storyteller), as it grew from the storytelling tradition of temple bards.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Kathak is marked by intricate footwork (tatkar), rapid spins (chakkars) and expressive abhinaya; it developed under both temple and Mughal court patronage and thus blends Hindu and Persian elements.

• Its main gharanas are Lucknow, Jaipur, Banaras and Raigarh. Famous exponents: Birju Maharaj, Sitara Devi, Shovana Narayan, Gopi Krishna.

NOTE

• Classical dances and their states: Bharatanatyam – Tamil Nadu; Kathak – Uttar Pradesh; Kathakali & Mohiniyattam – Kerala; Kuchipudi – Andhra Pradesh; Odissi – Odisha; Manipuri – Manipur; Sattriya – Assam.

question: In which of the following cities was the final match of the 2022 Vijay Hazare Trophy held?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ahmedabad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The final of the 2022 Vijay Hazare Trophy was played at the Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad (Gujarat), where Saurashtra defeated Maharashtra to lift the title. (विजय हजारे ट्रॉफी फाइनल — अहमदाबाद)

• The Vijay Hazare Trophy is India's premier domestic List-A (50-over) tournament for state teams, organised by the BCCI since 2002–03.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The trophy is named after the legendary Indian batsman Vijay Hazare, the first Indian to score a century in each innings of a Test.

• The Narendra Modi Stadium at Motera, Ahmedabad, is the largest cricket stadium in the world by capacity (about 1,32,000).

NOTE

• Major Indian domestic tournaments: Ranji Trophy (first-class), Duleep Trophy (zonal first-class), Irani Cup (Ranji champion vs Rest of India), Vijay Hazare Trophy (50 overs) and Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy (T20).

question: Who started the chemical revolution in the 18th century by naming oxygen and helping to organize chemical nomenclature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Antoine-Laurent Lavoisier, the French scientist known as the "Father of Modern Chemistry", started the chemical revolution in the 18th century. He named oxygen (1778) and hydrogen, disproved the phlogiston theory and helped systematise chemical nomenclature. (आधुनिक रसायन विज्ञान के जनक)

• He also formulated the Law of Conservation of Mass — matter can neither be created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Joseph Priestley actually discovered oxygen (1774) as "dephlogisticated air", but it was Lavoisier who named and correctly explained it.

• Svante August Arrhenius — Swedish scientist, gave the theory of electrolytic dissociation and won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry (1903).

• Dame Kathleen Lonsdale — Irish-British crystallographer who proved that the benzene ring is flat.

NOTE

• Lavoisier's book "Traité Élémentaire de Chimie (1789)" is regarded as the first modern chemistry textbook. He was executed during the French Revolution (1794).

question: Aman Sehrawat became the first Indian to win a gold medal in World Wrestling Championship in which category?
solution_text:
The correct answer is U-23.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Aman Sehrawat became the first Indian ever to win a gold medal at the U-23 World Wrestling Championships, winning in the 57 kg freestyle category in 2022 (Pontevedra, Spain). (अमन सहरावत — अंडर-23 विश्व कुश्ती चैंपियनशिप)

• He hails from Birohar village, Jhajjar district, Haryana, and trains at the Chhatrasal Stadium, Delhi.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Aman Sehrawat also won the Asian Championship gold (2023) and later became an Olympic medallist, winning bronze in the 57 kg freestyle at the Paris Olympics 2024.

• World wrestling is governed by the United World Wrestling (UWW); wrestling styles are freestyle and Greco-Roman.

NOTE

• Indian wrestling icons: Sushil Kumar (World Champion 2010; two Olympic medals), Bajrang Punia, Ravi Dahiya, Sakshi Malik (first Indian woman wrestler to win an Olympic medal) and Vinesh Phogat.

question: Independence Day is celebrated every year in Pakistan on ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 14 August.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pakistan celebrates its Independence Day (Yaum-e-Azadi) every year on 14 August, marking its creation in 1947 under the Indian Independence Act, 1947. (पाकिस्तान का स्वतंत्रता दिवस — 14 अगस्त)

• India became independent on 15 August 1947. The Radcliffe Line, drawn by Sir Cyril Radcliffe, demarcated the boundary between the two countries.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• 23 March is celebrated in Pakistan as "Pakistan Day / Republic Day", commemorating the Lahore Resolution of 1940.

• Pakistan's first Governor-General was Muhammad Ali Jinnah and its first Prime Minister was Liaquat Ali Khan. India's last Viceroy, Lord Mountbatten, oversaw the transfer of power.

question: Which of the following Indian musicians was called ‘Mallika-e-Ghazal’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Begum Akhtar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Begum Akhtar (1914–1974), born Akhtari Bai Faizabadi, was honoured with the title "Mallika-e-Ghazal" (the Queen of Ghazal). (मल्लिका-ए-ग़ज़ल — बेगम अख्तर)

• She was celebrated for her renditions of the ghazal, dadra and thumri, sung in a deeply emotive, semi-classical style.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, the Padma Shri (1968) and the Padma Bhushan posthumously (1975).

• Farida Khanum is a celebrated Pakistani ghazal singer (famous for "Aaj Jaane Ki Zid Na Karo"); Chitra Singh sang with Jagjit Singh.

NOTE

• A "ghazal" is a poetic form of couplets (sher) with a common rhyme (radif/qafia), of Persian origin. Famous ghazal exponents in India: Mehdi Hassan, Ghulam Ali, Jagjit Singh and Talat Aziz.

question: The word ‘yorker’ is related to which sport?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cricket.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "yorker" is a term from cricket. It is a delivery that pitches right at the batsman's feet or at the base of the stumps, making it very difficult to play — a favourite weapon of fast bowlers, especially in the death overs. (यॉर्कर — क्रिकेट)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other cricket terms: googly, bouncer, doosra, no-ball, wide, LBW, maiden over, hat-trick, silly point, follow-on, duck, stumping.

• Cricket is governed by the International Cricket Council (ICC), headquartered at Dubai; the laws of cricket are framed by the MCC (Marylebone Cricket Club), London.

NOTE

• Terms of other games: Kho Kho — pole, chain, sitting block; Kabaddi — raider, antis, lona, bonus point; Basketball — dribble, dunk, rebound, free throw, foul.
